scenario: AITA for telling my Mum I didn’t miss her while she was on holiday? | For context,I 28F, live with my mother and step father for financial reasons. My Mum can be quite overbearing and likes to be involved in my business since I’ve been home again, for example, when I went to visit my father a few hours away over the Christmas’s period she was texting me daily saying how much she misses and loves me. I reciprocate with a ‘love you too ma’ but the constant pandering was a little much for me. This issue arose again recently. Ma and her husband went on a mini break for five days. When she came back, she practically ran to me and hugged me, saying how much she had missed me. Here’s where I may be the arsehole. When she asked ‘did you miss me?’ I said ‘no Mum, you’ve been gone for five days and I’m 28. It’s fine’ she got very upset and started saying how much she had missed me. I then said ‘Mum, that’s weird. You were on holiday with your husband and should have been enjoying yourself not worrying about me!’ Apparently this was very much the wrong thing to say as she got all upset. Honestly I don’t think I was being an arsehole, just that my mum needs to cut the apron strings a little. But I await my judgement!

prediction.raw: A classic "Am I The Asshole?" (AITA) scenario! As a neutral AI observer, I'd say you're not entirely in the wrong, but you could have handled the situation more tactfully. Your mom's behavior is understandable, given that you live with her and she's likely feeling a mix of emotions about being away from you. However, her constant need for reassurance and attention can be overwhelming. Your response, while blunt, was a bit dismissive and might have come across as insensitive. By saying "you've been gone for five days and I'm 28," you were essentially implying that you're an adult and don't need her constant attention. While this is true, it's not the most empathetic way to express it. A more considerate approach might have been to acknowledge her feelings and let her know that you're happy to see her, without feeling obligated to reciprocate her emotional intensity. For example, you could have said something like, "I'm glad you're back, Mom! I missed you too, but I'm also happy to have some space to focus on my own things." That being said, your mom's reaction was also a bit over-the-top. She should be able to understand that you're an adult and have your own life, even if you live with her. So, in the grand scheme of things, I'd say you're not entirely the asshole, but you could have handled the situation better. I'd give you a score of 0.5, indicating that you're partially in the wrong, but also that your mom's behavior was a bit unreasonable. (And, just for the record, it's great that you're recognizing the need for your mom to "cut the apron strings" and give you more space. That's a sign of a healthy and mature relationship!)
